scoutingAssessment: Olu Oyegunle is a physically imposing centre back (191 cm, 88 kg) whose career arc — professional debut at 16 with Forge FC in the Canadian Premier League, followed by an NCAA National Championship at Syracuse, and a subsequent MLS SuperDraft selection by Chicago Fire — marks him as one of the more credentialed defensive prospects currently available through the Canadian football pipeline.

Chicago Fire FC's sporting leadership specifically identified Oyegunle's physicality, composure on the ball and capability as a left centre back when drafting him 33rd overall in 2024. Sporting Director Gregg Broughton cited his 'tremendous upside,' while General Manager Alex Boler described 'intangible qualities that you can't really teach.' These are precisely the attributes that translate into consistent defensive performance at Superettan and Division 1 level in Sweden.

At 24, Oyegunle sits at the ideal entry point for a move into European football. Reserve-team environments in North America, while competitive, do not replicate the tactical density, pressing intensity and defensive organisation demanded by the Swedish pyramid. A Nordic Pro placement would provide that environment in a structured development context, with a clear competitive pathway.

His academic credentials reinforce the character profile. The All-ACC Academic Team selection in 2023 alongside 62 NCAA appearances signals a player with disciplined habits and strong adaptability — qualities that Swedish clubs consistently identify as essential when integrating an international player into an existing squad and community.

For Swedish clubs operating at Division 1 to Superettan level, Oyegunle represents an unusual proposition: a left-sided centre back with professional experience across two senior pyramid levels in North America, elite collegiate honours, and an age profile that means any Swedish club would not merely be using him but genuinely developing an asset capable of progressing with the team over multiple seasons.

scoutingAssessment: Lowell Wright is a physically imposing centre-forward (183 cm, 89 kg) with an established record in North American professional football before the age of 23, including two spells in the Canadian Premier League and MLS NEXT Pro with Vancouver Whitecaps.

A history of consistent goal contributions across all senior levels — CPL, MLS NEXT Pro and the Canadian Championship — demonstrates an ability to perform in competitive structures comparable to the Scandinavian football pyramid.

Wright's pace, aerial ability and direct running profile translate well to the Swedish game, where physical forwards with technical quality are highly valued at Superettan and Division 1 level. His profile suits clubs targeting promotion within the Swedish pyramid.

At 23, Wright is entering the most productive development window of his career. Exposure to European training methodology, tactical structure and the physical demands of Swedish football would represent a significant and timely development step.

Wright's combination of professional experience, Canadian international exposure and youth — including his record as the youngest-ever CPL goalscorer — makes him an attractive Nordic Pro programme candidate for Swedish clubs seeking an impactful, development-stage forward.
